thread.title: Malaysia Shares May Erase Thursday's Losses

title: Malaysia Shares May Erase Thursday's Losses
text:
Malaysia Shares May Erase Thursday's Losses September 27, 2018, 07:30: The Malaysia stock market turned barely lower again on Thursday, one session after it had ended the two-day slide in which it had fallen more than 15 points or 0.8 percent. The Kuala Lumpur Composite Index now remains beneath the 1,800-point plateau although it's predicted to rebound on Friday.
The global forecast for the Asian markets is firm, with support expected from the oil and technology stocks. The European and U.S. markets were up and the Asian bourses are tipped to follow suit.
The KLCI finished barely lower on Thursday following losses from the telecoms, slim gains from the plantations and a mixed picture from the financials.
For the day, the index eased 0.08 points to finish at 1,798.64 after trading between 1,793.83 and 1,803.71. Volume was 2 billion shares worth 2 billion ringgit. There were 503 decliners and 359 gainers.
Among the actives, IHH Healthcare plummeted 2.08 percent, while Genting Malaysia surged 1.62 percent, Telekom Malaysia plunged 0.92 percent, Sime Darby spiked 0.76 percent, IOI Corporation jumped 0.44 percent, Petronas Chemicals climbed 0.43 percent, Dialog Group advanced 0.29 percent, CIMB Group skidded 0.17 percent, Tenaga Nasional added 0.13 percent, Maybank collected 0.10 percent, Kuala Lumpur Kepong gained 0.08 percent and Digi.com, RHB Capital, Malaysia Airports Holdings, Public Bank and Petronas Gas all were unchanged.
The lead from Wall Street is upbeat as stocks opened higher on Thursday. They faded slightly in the afternoon but still finished firmly in the green.
The Dow added 54.65 points or 0.21 percent to 26,439.93, while the NASDAQ gained 51.60 points or 0.65 percent to 8,041.97 and the S&P was up 8.03 points or 0.28 percent to 2,914.00.
A notable advance by shares of Apple (AAPL) contributed to the higher close on Wall Street after J.P. Morgan initiated coverage of the company's stock with an Overweight rating.
In economic news, the Commerce Department noted a bigger than expected jump in durable goods orders in August. The Commerce Department also said the pace of U.S. economic growth in the second quarter was unrevised at 4.2 percent from the previous estimate.
Also, the Labor Department noted a rebound in initial jobless claims in the week ended September 22. And the National Association of Realtors said pending home sales dropped much more than expected in August.
Crude oil prices moved higher on Thursday, amid concerns that sanctions on Iran from November may result in supply shortage in the market. Crude oil futures for November delivery ended up $0.55 or 0.8 percent at $72.12 a barrel. //www.rttnews.com/2938880/malaysia-shares-may-erase-thursday-s-losses.aspx
